tagline: Eight miles of forest gravel where settlers once tapped maples.
intro: From Cassville the drive heads south on Highway 112 through Roaring River State Park, then turns off onto Forest Road 197. There the pavement gives way to eight miles of gravel that go deeper into the woods at every turn, over hills of mixed hardwoods with red cedar and pine. The gravel comes out on Highway 86 near Table Rock Lake, and the paved road winds back through more forest toward Cassville.
The name comes from the sugar maples along the way, which settlers once tapped for syrup.

moments.title: Roaring River State Park
moments.text: The park began as 2,400 acres bought and handed to the state by a medicine-show man who made millions selling patent medicines and soap from traveling tent shows.

moments.title: Sugar Camp Lookout Tower
moments.text: Up Forest Road 1004 stands a fire tower the Civilian Conservation Corps built in the 1930s, with one picnic table and a rule against climbing.

moments.title: Onyx Observation Area
moments.text: About a mile and a half on, a small pull-off with two picnic tables looks out over the Ozark Highlands.

practical: The eight-mile middle section on Forest Road 197 is maintained gravel. There is no potable water at the tower or the Onyx pull-off.

sources.label: USDA Forest Service, Mark Twain National Forest, Sugar Camp National Forest Scenic Byway
